title: Strawberry ice cream
subtitle: Fresh strawberry custard ice cream
excerpt: A proper strawberry ice cream: a cooked egg yolk custard base churned with a fresh strawberry puree. Pink, creamy, and intensely fruity. Best made at the height of strawberry season.
sourceNotes: Classic French-style custard ice cream (glace à la crème) applied to British strawberries. Technique cross-referenced with Jeni Britton Bauer, Jeni's Splendid Ice Creams at Home (2011) for stabilisation rationale; custard base proportions follow the standard crème anglaise ratio.

recipe.freezeNotes: Store in a sealed container in the freezer for up to 6 weeks. Press a sheet of baking parchment against the surface to prevent ice crystals.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The custard base must be chilled completely before churning (at least 4 hours, or overnight).

glossaryTerms.definition: A pourable egg yolk and cream custard sauce; the base for most custard ice creams. Cooked gently until it coats the back of a spoon.

content.text: A strawberry ice cream made with fresh strawberries and a proper crème anglaise custard base is noticeably better than a no-cook version. The custard gives body and richness; the strawberry puree gives freshness and fruit flavour. You need ripe, sweet strawberries; pale, out-of-season fruit gives a flat-tasting result.

Blend the strawberries with the 50 g caster sugar and lemon juice until smooth. Taste: it should be slightly over-sweet, as freezing dulls sweetness. Press through a sieve to remove the seeds. Refrigerate until cold.
Heat the cream and milk in a saucepan until just below boiling point. Meanwhile, whisk the egg yolks, 80 g sugar, and vanilla in a bowl until pale and slightly thickened.

Pour the hot cream mixture over the yolks in a slow stream, whisking constantly. Return to the saucepan and cook over low heat, stirring with a wooden spoon, until the crème anglaise thickens enough to coat the back of the spoon (about 82°C). Do not let it boil.
Pour through a sieve into a clean bowl and stir in the cold strawberry puree. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours until completely cold.

Churn in an ice cream machine according to the manufacturer's instructions until thick and creamy, about 20 to 25 minutes. Transfer to a lidded container and freeze for at least 2 hours before serving.
Remove from the freezer 5 minutes before serving to soften slightly.

items.symptom: The custard scrambled (curdled) in the pan
items.cause: Heat too high or not stirred continuously
items.fix: Immediately pour through a fine sieve into a cold bowl and blend. If the texture is only slightly grainy it is usually recoverable. Cook on the lowest heat next time.

items.symptom: The ice cream is icy and grainy
items.cause: The custard was not cold enough before churning, or the machine bowl was not frozen
items.fix: Chill the mixture overnight. Ensure the ice cream machine bowl is frozen solid (usually 24 hours in the freezer).

items.symptom: The ice cream is very hard to scoop
items.cause: Too much water content or not enough sugar/fat
items.fix: Let it sit at room temperature for 5 to 10 minutes before scooping. This recipe is calibrated for good scoopability.
Use only genuinely ripe, sweet strawberries. Macerate them with the sugar for 30 minutes before blending to intensify the flavour.

content.text: Strawberry ice cream is British summer in a scoop. The combination of custard base and fresh fruit is the foundation of every classic ice cream parlour; egg yolks are what distinguish a real ice cream from a simple frozen cream. June and July are the months for this: English strawberries at their best, picked when fully ripe. Serve in wafer cones or plain in a chilled glass with a little cream poured over.
